title: Daily visual schedule for developmental disabilities | ELUM
description: How to show the day ahead in pictures for kids with developmental disabilities or autism: making a picture schedule, handling changes, and examples.
keywords: autism visual schedule, picture schedule for autism, developmental disability routine, daily routine for autistic child, visual schedule for developmental disabilities, preparing for changes in routine
heading: Developmental disabilities and a daily schedule: show it ahead in pictures
lede: Knowing what comes next can make the whole day feel calmer.

sections.heading: Knowing ahead helps
paragraphs: Some people find pictures and order easier to understand than words or speech. When you show the day in pictures, your child can check for themselves what to do, what comes next and when it ends.
Hearing "time to go" out of nowhere feels very different from having seen the next step on a card ahead of time.

sections.heading: Steps to make a daily schedule
list: Split the day into a few parts. Getting ready in the morning, going to school, coming home, bedtime
Make each part a routine. 3 to 6 cards per routine
Only one action per card. Use the same pictures every time so they become familiar
Use the read-aloud voice too. Hearing the same sentence in the same voice makes it easier to understand
Add a reward at the end. It makes the end of the routine clear

sections.heading: When plans change
paragraphs: For days that are different from usual, like a doctor's visit or guests coming over, show the cards the day before. For a new place, it helps to lay out in order what will happen there and when it ends.
In ELUM, write something like "going for a vaccination tomorrow," and ELUM breaks it into steps that fit the situation and makes cards.

sections.heading: You decide
paragraphs: ELUM does not ask for a diagnosis or type of disability. You know your child best, including what's easy and what's hard. Cards made by AI are shown only after you edit and check them.

cards.title: Action card example: getting ready for bed

faq.q: What kind of pictures work best?
faq.a: It's different for everyone. Some find simple pictures like emoji or picture symbols easier, and others prefer pictures that look like the real thing. In ELUM, you can choose from four picture styles.

faq.q: Can we use it at school or a center too?
faq.a: Yes. You can invite another caregiver to see your child's routines together, and you can print cards or send them as images.
